context: A hive plot with 80 nodes on 3 structural axes (Sources/Connectors/Sinks) and ~142 directed edges, using a colorblind-safe 3-color Tol palette, keyboard-navigable with screen reader support and a hover/click detail panel.
first_impression: The three-axis structure imposes clear organization and the restrained palette reads immediately, but the dense bundle of curves converging at center makes the default state look busier than it is.
what_works: The 3-color Tol palette (blue/red/green) separates axes instantly and stays distinguishable at all node sizes; the click-to-highlight interaction — dimming unrelated edges to 0.03 opacity — effectively transforms an ambiguous tangle into a legible ego-network on demand.
what_doesnt: In the unselected default state, ~142 overlapping quadratic curves create a congested center mass that requires interaction to parse — a viewer who doesn't hover or click gets limited structural insight; the 30-node Source axis is also dense enough that small nodes near the outer end begin to overlap, making individual node selection by pointer imprecise.
